transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-11-29 15:00 UTC 
Duration: 58 minutes 
Attendees: Maya Chen (AE), Liam O'Connor (SE) - Redwood; Priya Desai (Head of ML), Carlos Mendez (SRE Lead), Aisha Malik (Security Manager), Tom Reynolds (VP Product) - Springboard Health

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): quick health check, discuss last week's latency bump, patching for autoscale, security follow-up re: KMS and audit logs, plan short pilot for quantized model on Dedicated capacity.

00:00 Maya: hi everyone thanks for joining, Maya from Redwood. we have Liam on the call our solutions engineer. how's it going at springboard?
00:08 Tom: hey Maya, yeah busy but good. we wanted to talk through a couple things - we saw a latency blip last week during the noon spike and costs crept up. also Aisha had follow-ups on security docs.
00:18 Maya: got it. quick agenda: usage/costs, latency root cause, security/retention, pilot scope and timeline. ok?
00:24 Priya: yep that's us. also want to see if a quantized variant will keep our quality bar for triage scoring - we can't lose recall on the top-3.
00:31 Liam: great, thanks. Carlos you ran the initial tail analysis? what did you see?
00:37 Carlos: yeah I pulled traces. p95 jumped from 240ms to ~520ms at around 12:10 local on 11/22. p99 was spiky to 1.2s. looks correlated with a batch of long-context requests, about 30% longer seq. our autoscale didn't react fast enough, and we had a cache miss storm — the prefix cache didn't warm because sequence prefixes changed. also noticed some retries from our side making the tail worse.
01:05 Maya: interesting, so two levers: reduce cold cache misses and tighten autoscale reaction. Redwood has the autoscale hysteresis settings and prefix-level caching we can tune. Liam can you mention the quick wins?
01:15 Liam: yeah, quick wins are: 1) tune the autoscale policy to be more sensitive to concurrent open streams (reduce scale-down aggressiveness), 2) enable prefix prefetching on paths that are high variance, 3) use a small warm pool during known noon windows. all three reduce p99 without big cost delta. we can estimate the token cost delta once we have the traffic sample.
01:40 Priya: cost is the big one for us. our finance noticed a 18% month-over-month increase and they want a clear plan to cap burn. are there specific quantization or batching knobs to lower per-token $ without hurting QA?
01:50 Liam: yes — we recommend a staged approach: run 4-bit quantized candidate models on Dedicated for benchmarking (ours supports quant profiles), and enable workload-aware batching (Redwood Optimize suggestions). in many production triage workloads we see 20-35% cost reduction with negligible top-K metric drift after careful eval.
02:11 Tom: top-K drift concern is real. Priya, do we have defined acceptance thresholds?
02:15 Priya: yes, top-3 recall must be >= 98% of current baseline, FNR can't increase more than 1.5 percentage points, and latency p95 must not exceed 400ms for the triage path.
02:28 Liam: perfect, we'll run replay bench and report p50/p95/p99, token cost, and a simple quality compare using your prompt set.
02:36 Aisha: quick security questions — we need to confirm KMS key management, whether keys are customer-managed, and whether audit logs include per-request metadata for 90 days. also SSO and RBAC requirements.
02:47 Maya: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. Hosted still has Redwood-managed keys by default but we can discuss bring-your-own-key for Dedicated/private control plane. audit logs are available and can be exported to your SIEM; retention is configurable. I'll send the security pack with diagrams.
03:06 Aisha: any info on how audit logs redact PII and what fields are stored, e.g., prompt hashes vs raw prompts?
03:12 Liam: good question. by default we store prompts as encrypted blobs but we can configure hashing for privacy-preserving auditing. the security pack details fields; we'll call out recommended settings for regulated workloads.
03:24 Carlos: back to ops, I'm worried about bursty long-context traffic. is there a way to route long context requests to a different variant to protect latency for short requests?
03:32 Liam: yes that's a common pattern: smart routing by request policy. route long-context to a higher-memory but slower-throughput model, and keep low-latency small-context requests on the fast path. Redwood routing can do this by route rules or by request headers. fallback policies can be set if the long-context pool is saturated.
03:49 Priya: will that increase cost? we need to quantify.
03:52 Liam: it can increase cost per long-request but protects overall latency SLO and reduces retries which actually can reduce total token cost. with the replay we can estimate overall spend delta for your mix.
04:05 Tom: timeline question — how long to validate quantized candidate?
04:09 Liam: assuming you provide prompt set and a 48h traffic slice, Redwood can run replay bench on Dedicated within 48–72 hours, then a 2-week sanity pilot if you're happy with numbers. so roughly 3 weeks end-to-end for an initial roll decision.
04:24 Priya: ok that works with our quarter goals. one more thing: we need an exec summary for finance that shows cost delta and risk.
04:30 Maya: we'll produce a one-page runbook: baseline economics, projected savings, risk matrix, and rollback plan.
04:37 Aisha: regarding compliance, do you have SOC2 + ISO? our legal requires copies.
04:41 Maya: yes SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 — I'll attach certs. also we have a compliance whitepaper that explains KMS and network isolation for Dedicated/VPC.
04:50 Carlos: can you confirm whether Dedicated runbooks integrate with our PagerDuty? we want alerting on capacity approaching headroom.
04:56 Liam: yes we support webhooks, Datadog, and PD. we can push custom metrics like pool utilization and predicted scale events.
05:03 Tom: any known issues or product deprecations coming that would affect us?
05:07 Maya: nothing breaking in the next quarter. some minor UX updates to the Console, and an upcoming optimizer for batching heuristics, but no incompatible changes. we'll notify early.
05:16 Priya: good. can we talk about the price side — if we move some traffic to Dedicated, how does the billing work, and can we reserve capacity?
05:23 Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity model: monthly commit with options for burst to hosted for rare overages. we can model run-rate savings vs hosted pay-as-you-go. our pricing team will share example scenarios once we have the replay bench numbers.
05:36 Carlos: for the bench, what exact artifacts do you need from us?
05:40 Liam: ideally: 1) representative prompt set (50–200 prompts covering edge cases), 2) 48–72 hour traffic slice with timestamps and request/response sizes (anonymized), and 3) your evaluation metric script or instructions for top-3 recall compare.
05:58 Priya: we'll anonymize and share the traffic slice and the eval script. I'll own that action.
06:06 Maya: perfect. i'll send a calendar invite for the follow-up tech deep dive week of Dec 11; we'll include extended SEs.
06:13 Tom: sounds good. any blockers on Redwood side for provisioning a trial Dedicated pool?
06:18 Maya: none — we can provision a trial capacity for benchmarking within 24–48 hours after we agree the scope. I'll coordinate with our infra team.
06:25 Aisha: one more compliance detail — do you support customer-managed subnets for Dedicated when deployed in our VPC?
06:31 Liam: yes, Dedicated in VPC mode supports customer-subnet configuration and egress rules. we'll provide the network checklist.
06:38 Priya: ok great. quick recap?
06:40 Maya: recap: Redwood will provision Dedicated trial, run a 48h replay bench with a 4-bit quant profile, produce p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost delta plus a simple quality comparison. Customer to provide prompt set, traffic slice, and retention requirement for audit logs. Security docs exchanged. Follow-up tech review week of 2028-12-11.
06:58 Tom: thanks everyone. we'll aim to get artifacts to you by Dec 6.
07:02 Maya: thanks all, end.
